fix(backend): set Django up off uvicorn's event loop (#2572)

HttpServer runs request handlers off the Netty event loop, on a per-server virtual-thread executor shut down with the server: a handler that calls back into its own server could be assigned the same busy loop thread and hang until the read timeout (the karate-ext console re-sending to its own demo API). Each connection chains its answers, so a later request's handler starts only after the earlier response is written (a delayed response included) and reads resume when the queue drains; requests are fully copied before dispatch; WebSocket/SSE and the 400 path stay on the loop; an error still answers 500. HttpServer.Builder.workerThreads(int) for sizing the loop. HttpServerReentrantHandlerTest (worker loop of 1, both failing first): a reentrant call answers, and pipelined /slow then /fast answer in order. karate-js 1801/0/0 (2 skipped), karate-core 2803/0/0 (3 skipped).

A Suite owns the mock servers karate.start() opens during it and stops them at the end of Suite.run() (after features, ext onShutdown and result listeners, in the finally, so an aborted run stops them too): a config or callSingle-started mock no longer outlives its Suite, so repeated runs in one JVM stop leaking servers and threads. A server started inside callSingle under a host-injected shared cache is left to that cache, which serves every Suite sharing it. Suite.ownServer / Suite.detachServers let a host that keeps a finished runtime take the servers over (DESIGN.md §"Suite isolation"). SuiteMockServerTest (4, three failing first): the mock is stopped at Suite end, two concurrent Suites each stop only their own, detach transfers ownership, a shared-cache mock survives.
